text:
Introduction and purpose of the document

1: This document sets out the principles and features of our funding system for the 2026 to 2027 funding year (1 August to 31 July) for Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) funded adult skills fund (ASF) delivery. We may make changes to these principles and features during the funding year.

2: This document describes how we calculate ‘formula-funded’ earnings for DWP funded ASF and learning support. We define ‘formula-funded’ activity as that recorded under funding model:

38 (‘adult skills fund’) for aims started on or after 1 August 2024

35 (‘adult skills’) for aims started prior to 1 August 2024

3: All learning aims with a start date or original start date prior to 1 August 2024 continuing into the year 2026 to 2027 should continue being recorded in the individualised learner record (ILR) using funding model 35 (‘adult skills’). We will continue to use the funding calculation from 2023 to 2024 for these learning aims.

4: This document does not include or describe:

devolved delivery - for more information on devolved/delegated delivery, refer to the devolution of the adult skills fund section

the ‘non-formula-funded’ activity within DWP funded ASF which is reconciled through the funding claims process (this includes non-regulated learning recorded under tailored learning (funding model 11)) - for more information on funding claims and tailored learning, refer to the Adult skills fund: funding rules

5: To understand how our funding system works, read this document together with the:

Adult skills fund: funding rules

ILR specification

provider support manual

Understanding our terminology

6: The term ‘we’ or ‘us’ refers to DWP or the Department for Education (DfE).

7: When we refer to ‘you’ or ‘providers’, this includes colleges, higher education institutions, training organisations, local authorities and employers that receive funding from us to deliver education and training.

What’s new in this guidance for 2026 to 2027?

8: Responsibility for adult skills fund policy transferred to DWP on 16 September 2025. DfE continues to implement the ASF on behalf of DWP. Throughout this document, references to the DfE have been updated to reflect this change and now refer to the DWP where appropriate.

9: We have clarified the guidance around claiming additional funding for the King’s Trust. More details can be found in paragraph 76.

10: From 1 August 2026 we will fund construction skills certification scheme (CSCS) cards for construction workers undertaking specific construction related learning aims, including free courses for jobs (FCFJ) learning aims. More details can be found in paragraph 83 and in the Adult skills fund: funding rules.

11: We have removed references to community learning (funding model 10) for 2026 to 2027 as these are no longer recorded in the ILR 2026 to 2027.

12: We have changed the way you pay back funding relating to the funding rules monitoring report (FRM27 - Continuing or completed learning aims that are now reported as withdrawn on or before 31 July of the previous funding year). Do not use the earnings adjustment statement (EAS) to pay this back. More details can be found in the section Recording late data in the ILR.

Devolution of the adult skills fund

13: The government agreed a series of devolution deals between central government and local areas in England. Throughout this guidance we refer to these as Strategic Authorities (SAs) as described in the English Devolution White paper. SAs have the responsibility to ensure eligible learners who reside in their area have appropriate education and training.

14: Providers with funding for devolved delivery from a SA will use the ILR again in the 2026 to 2027 funding year. The source of funding (SOF) codes identify the SA whose contract is funding these devolved learners.

15: We will provide funding reports for devolved delivery using our funding calculation. The detailed occupancy report will include the appropriate funding line type for the SA using the SOF field from the ILR collection. This report may form the basis on which the SA funds you, which could differ in amount or delivery methodology than that we use. Each SA will use their own systems and processes to pay you.

16: Refer to the ILR specification and the provider support manual for further details on recording devolved delivery.

The data we use to calculate funding

17: You give us information about learners and their learning using the ILR and the EAS. Our funding system uses this information to work out the funding you have earned for delivering this learning.

Our funding system features

18: Our funding system has the following 4 features, which are set out in more detail throughout this document:

the funding formula, including uplifts to the rates to account for the extra costs that you may experience when delivering learning to some types of learners and in some locations, or where there are skills shortages

the funding rates for learning aims and work placements

the earnings method, linked to delivery and achievement or completion

support funding where extra help is needed for learners to achieve

Our funding formula

Calculation

19: The funding formula is below which is unchanged from last year:

funding = rate x disadvantage uplift x area cost uplift

20: The basis for funding is the rate for the learning aim.

21: We adjust the funding formula to allow for geographical differences in the relative cost of delivery and to enable additional support for learners living in more disadvantaged areas. For further information see the disadvantage uplift and area cost uplift sections.

22: In some cases, we expect learners and employers to share responsibility for investing in eligible provision. We expect them to part-fund the cost of learning, known as co-funding. For more information on co-funding, refer to the ‘government contribution charts’ in the adult skills Adult skills fund: funding and performance management rules.

Disadvantage uplift

23: The disadvantage uplift provides extra funding to support the most disadvantaged learners, recognising that they are sometimes more costly to recruit and retain. We apply this consistently across DWP ‘formula-funded’ adult skills fund provision.

24: To calculate the disadvantage uplift for new starts from 1 August 2021 we use the index of multiple deprivation (IMD) 2019. This results in a funding increase for learners living in the most deprived areas of the country. We base the uplift on the learner’s postcode (based upon the ‘postcode prior to enrolment’ field in the ILR). If required the uplift factor is between 1.084 and 1.336, otherwise we default the factor to 1.

25: The method we use to calculate disadvantage factors from the IMD value is as follows:

IMD 2019 gives a value of relative deprivation for every lower layer super output area (LSOA) in England

we apply the uplift to learners living in the 27% most deprived LSOAs

the disadvantage uplift factor for the least deprived LSOA within that 27% is 1.084

the disadvantage uplift factor for the most deprived LSOA is 1.336

for LSOAs with IMD scores between those two points, we calculate disadvantage factors using a linear relationship within the 27% between the least deprived IMD score (28.324) and the most deprived IMD score (92.735), and their corresponding disadvantage factor values (1.084 and 1.336)

for example, an increase of the IMD score value by 6.4411 (one tenth of the range from 27% to the most deprived) would correspond to an increase in disadvantage factor of 0.0252 (one tenth of the difference between 1.084 and 1.336)

once we have a disadvantage factor for an LSOA, we apply it to all postcodes within that LSOA, using postcode data published by the Office for National Statistics

26: The disadvantage uplift factor at the start of the learning aim will apply throughout the duration of the learning aim.

27: SAs may wish to set different disadvantage factors to DWP for their ASF delivery each year. For FCFJ we calculate funding using DWP’s disadvantage factors, even when funded by a SA.

28: The disadvantage uplift factors are available at uplift factors and postcode files, this includes the SA factors. For more information about how the SAs set their factors, contact the relevant SA.

Area cost uplift

29: The area cost uplift reflects the higher cost of delivering training provision in some parts of the country, such as London and the South East. We apply this consistently across DWP’s ‘formula-funded’ ASF provision.

30: If this applies the uplift factor is between 1.01 and 1.20, otherwise we default the factor to 1. We base the uplift on the ‘delivery location postcode’ recorded in the ILR. As the delivery location of distance and e-learning provision is not set, we default the area uplift factor to 1. Annex 2 contains details of areas where we provide an area cost increase. The area cost uplift factors are available at uplift factors and postcode files.

31: The area cost uplift factor at the start of the learning aim will apply throughout the duration of the learning aim. The area cost factors in annex 2 are unchanged from last year.

Financial contributions

32: If a learner meets the criteria for full funding (refer to the Adult skills fund: funding rules for more information), you can claim the full rate for the qualification. For co-funded learners, we expect the learner or employer to contribute so we reduce the funding by 50% of the unweighted rate of the learning aim as shown in find a learning aim (FALA).

33: We reduce the funding using the unweighted rate because a learner should not contribute more for the same size of the learning aim just because that learning aim is more costly to deliver. This means that the government will contribute more towards learning aims with higher operational and delivery costs, such as engineering.

Recognition of prior learning

34: If you record data in the ‘funding adjustment for prior learning’ field on the ILR, we change the funding formula to reflect this. However, it does not change the fixed monthly learning support funding.

35: If the learning aim does not use the restart indicator, we reduce the achievement or completion funding as well as the monthly instalments. This is because we assume the learner has earned some achievement or completion within the prior learning.

36: If the learning aim uses the restart indicator, we reduce the monthly instalments, but the achievement or completion funding stays at 20% of the full funding rate.

Other funding adjustments

37: Where you have agreement with us to adjust DWP funding upwards for other reasons apart from prior learning, you must record it in the ‘other funding adjustment’ field in the ILR. You must not use this ILR field for DWP upward revisions if you do not have an agreement in place with us. We will monitor its use. However, you can use this to reduce funding without our agreement.

38: This ‘other funding adjustment’ factor increases or decreases the funding for that learning, including the achievement or completion funding. However, it does not change learning support funding.

39: If there is also a factor for prior learning recorded, we multiply the ‘funding adjustment for prior learning’ factor by the ‘other funding adjustment’ factor and apply it to the appropriate funding.

Our funding rates

Principles

40: The list of regulated qualifications approved for public funding are on find a learning aim that we update regularly. For information about what is eligible for public funding, refer to qualifications and public funding.

41: As rates can change between and during academic years (because of policy change or changes to the learning aim), we fund each learning aim at the rate that applies when the learner starts that learning aim. This principle is the same for a new start in the current funding year and a continuing learner from previous years. This rate will apply for the full duration of the learning aim and does not change between funding years.

42: The amount you earn recognises the relative value and costs of delivering provision in different sectors and subjects. We set the rates using the following criteria:

funded guided learning hours (GLH)

hourly rates that recognise the relative costs of delivering training in different sectors and subjects and provides a boost for training in those sectors identified as having greatest skills needs

Sector uplifts are based on the Sector Subject Area (SSA) that awarding organisations decide. The Register of Regulated Qualifications and the Access to Higher Education websites record the SSAs. Some components of qualifications can have multiple SSAs, where this happens, we set the SSA.

43: We have some exceptions that do not use the criteria above. In these instances, we set rates for some policy areas and specific learning aims such as:

work experience

HGV medical

HGV certificates of competence

CSCS cards

44: We add an uplift to the rate for all learners on FCFJ, more details can be found in paragraph 71.

45: We refer to rates as ‘unweighted’ when calculated using the base rate of £6.00 per hour. Once we have calculated the rate using the appropriate skills funding band, we refer to it as the ‘weighted rate’. After we apply the uplifts, we refer to the ‘aim value’, as noted in the ‘main occupancy report’. For more information on funding reports see the funding reports section.

46: All rates shown on find a learning aim are fully funded rates for learners aged 19 and above. We adjust these rates through the funding formula according to our policy (for example, if the government contributes only part of the full rate).

47: All learners funded through the 16 to 19 funding model that turned 19 in their second or subsequent funding year of a single programme of study are funded through the 16 to 19 funding model.

48: Our rates do not change depending on how you deliver the learning (for example, by delivering it on-line compared to in the classroom). Where rates are based on GLH, the rate is always the funded GLH in FALA regardless of how many hours you deliver the learning in.

Funding rates

49: We fund each GLH that is assigned to the qualification at an hourly rate, depending on the skills funding band assigned to the SSA of the qualification (see table 1). Each qualification is funded according to the specific GLH and SSA assigned to the qualification. Where a learning aim had a rate set in 2025 to 2026 (or earlier) and is continuing into 2026 to 2027, this rate remains unchanged for 2026 to 2027.

50: SAs are responsible for setting their own funding rates, where they do so these rates will form the basis of the funding calculation for provision funded by SAs and will be displayed in FALA.

51: Funding rates for individual qualifications are determined by multiplying the relevant hourly rate for the SSA of the qualification by the number of GLH as assigned by the awarding organisation and recorded on Ofqual’s register of regulated qualifications.

52: We use the GLH assigned by the awarding organisation and as recorded in Ofqual’s register. Where an awarding organisation amends the GLH for a qualification on Ofqual’s register, we may not automatically reflect this change in the associated funding rate. Therefore, there may be a difference between the GLH recorded on Ofqual’s register and the GLH we are using for the funding rate.

53: FALA shows the funded GLH in addition to the Ofqual GLH, so it is clear where there is a difference.

54: The Quality Assurance Agency for Higher Education (QAA) regulates Access to Higher Education Diplomas. The GLH for these qualifications is set at 600 hours.

Skills funding bands

55: Each SSA at tier 2 level is assigned to one of the 5 funding bands, see table 1. The funding bands for each SSA tier 2 are set out in annex 1.

56: We set all unweighted rates using the base rate of £6.00 per hour.

Table 1: adult skills funding rates by band

Adult skills funding band Base Low Medium High Specialist

Hourly adult skills funding rate £6.00 £7.20 £8.40 £9.60 £12.00

57: Here is an example of how we set rates taking Learning aim reference 60008817 Diploma in Engineering with funded GLH of 360:

The unweighted rate is calculated by multiplying the funded GLH of 360 by the base rate of £6.00 - this gives an unweighted funding rate of £2,160.

The weighted rate is calculated by multiplying the funded GLH of 360 by £9.60 (which is the hourly adult skills funding rate for high funding band that engineering SSA is in) - this gives a weighted funding rate of £3,456.

58: The following policy exceptions remain for these qualifications:

English GCSEs are funded within the low funding band rather than the base funding rate band - this means they get a funding rate of £864 in line with the GLH of 120 and in line with the funding rate for maths GCSE

functional skills in English entry level, level 1 and level 2, receive the current policy rate of £724

functional skills in maths entry level, are funded at the policy rate of £941, and level 1 and level 2 at £724

we fund digital functional skills qualifications under a different SSA’s funding band. We treat these as if they are in the digital technology (users) SSA from 2024 to 2025 - this means the funding rate for digital functional skills qualifications is £462 (the new hourly skills funding rate for digital technology (users) SSA is £8.40 and GLH for these qualifications is 55 hours)

59: If you offer English for speakers of other languages (ESOL) qualifications, you may need to deliver additional learning to individual learners that incurs additional costs above the qualification rate. Where additional hours are required, you can record these on the ILR as detailed in the ILR specification and the provider support manual.

60: The steps for claiming top-up for an ESOL qualification are:

Identify the funded GLH of the ESOL qualification through FALA.

Work out the additional delivery hours you need to complete the learning - this is the 100 planned hours minus the funded GLH value of the ESOL qualification.

Record these hours using the ‘Hours Record: Entity’ in the ILR specification.

Use the attribute type ‘HRS’ and attribute code 6 - Additional Delivery Hours.

For example, you plan to deliver learning aim reference 60140070 Level 2 Award in ESOL Skills for Life (reading) in 100 hours which has:

funded GLH of 60

a skills funding rate of £360

The additional delivery hours required is 40 - the 100 planned hours minus the funded GLH value of the ESOL qualification.

In the ILR, record the amount of 40 as the HRSAmount against attribute type ‘HRS’ and attribute code 6.

The funding calculation automatically calculates the additional funding as 40 x £6.00 = £240. The overall rate is calculated as the original rate (£360) + the top up amount (£240) = £600.

Land-based qualifications

61: In adult provision, 3 SSAs include land-based qualifications:

agriculture (SSA T2 3.1)

horticulture and forestry (SSA T2 3.2)

animal care and veterinary science (SSA T2 3.3)

62: Funding for relevant land-based technical qualifications have the specialist funding band applied where all the following criteria are met:

providers have a ‘specialist status’ as set out in annex C of 16 to 19 funding: rates and formula

the qualifications within the 3 land-based SSAs do not meet any of the exceptions in the next paragraph

a specialist provider delivers a qualification at their land-based location that met specific and additional criteria within the 3 SSAs

If all 3 criteria are not met the provision will not be deemed specialist and will have the high funding band applied.

63: Specialist funding rate will apply to all technical level 2 and 3 qualifications, except for the following:

qualifications where employment is a pre-requisite, this is because the training aspects requiring specialist equipment can take place on the employer’s premises - qualifications linked to occupational regulation or a certificate of competence are an exception to this and are funded at the specialist funding rate

qualifications within animal care and veterinary science SSA which are solely focussed on domestic animal care

floristry qualifications within horticulture and forestry SSA as they do not require specialist provision

qualifications related to forest schools

qualifications related to garden design and planning

Work placement for 19 to 24 year olds

64: We identify work placement learning aims through find a learning aim using category code ‘Adult Skills Fund - Work Placement (code 74)’.

65: The work placement hours referred to in the learning aim title represent the length of the placement. You should choose the learning aim reference with the appropriate hours for the work placement. Each rate is intended to reflect the administration and support costs associated with those hours.

66: The minimum total length of work placement we fund for a single learner is 70 hours.

67: The maximum total length of work placements we fund for a single learner is 240 hours. For more information, refer to the Adult skills fund: funding rules.

68: The learning aims for work placement are shown in table 2.

Table 2: Adult skills funding rates by band

Learning aim reference Learning aim title Funding rate

Z0030000 Adult Skills Fund – Work Placement 70-80 hours £450

Z0030001 Adult Skills Fund – Work Placement 81-160 hours £724

Z0030002 Adult Skills Fund – Work Placement 161-240 hours £1,265

69: For work placement aims, we do not hold back 20% of the rate for achievement or completion. Instead, we apportion all the funding for the aim as monthly instalments.

70: There are some additional funding eligibility criteria for work placement learning aims which are described in the Adult skills fund: funding rules.

Free courses for jobs offer

71: Additional funding is available through free courses for jobs for adults who meet the eligibility criteria and are studying a qualification from the list of approved FCFJ qualifications. Eligibility is described in detail in the Adult skills fund: funding rules. We fund this learning as we fund other ASF delivery, with the following exceptions:

learners eligible for this offer are fully funded for their FCFJ learning aim

we increase the weighted rate by £600 for eligible aims in category code 45 (‘Free Courses for Jobs rate 1’) or by £150 for eligible aims in category code 46 (‘Free Courses for Jobs rate 2’)

we increase the £150 or £600 by the area cost uplift or disadvantage uplift if applicable to that learning aim

72: You should use the learning delivery and monitoring (LDM) code 378 (Free courses for jobs offer) for all FCFJ aims for both 19 to 23 and 24+ learners. This will ensure you earn funding for the £150 or £600 uplifts.

73: All FCFJ learning aims with LDM code 378, irrespective of age, are funded through your FCFJ funding line.

74: You should only use LDM code 382 when recording learners continuing their learning from funding year 2023 to 2024 who met the low wage eligibility criteria. SAs can also set their own wage threshold (below which adults with an existing Level 3 can access FCFJ). You must not use LDM code 382 for any starts on or after 1 August 2024.

75: For starts on or after 1 August 2026 Mayoral Strategic Authorities can set their own rates and uplifts for FCFJ qualifications. Foundation Strategic Authorities [FSAs] have some limited flexibility to use their ASF FCFJ allocation to fund additional qualifications which are not part of the national offer. The FSAs are responsible for notifying you about any qualifications where this flexibility applies. For these qualifications however, the funding calculation will not increase the weighted rate by £150 or £600.

King’s Trust team programme

76: The programme rate is the same as last year at £3,204. This programme rate is the same for both employed and unemployed learners. We do not apply uplifts for disadvantage and area cost to the programme rate.

77: You will earn the funding rate for the award or certificate in ‘Employment, Teamwork and Community Skills’. The qualifications you can use are in table 3. You must also record the learners on the ILR using the LDM code 331.

78: If the funding rate is lower than the programme rate, you can claim additional funding from the qualification rate up to the value of the programme rate. To claim this additional funding, you must use the Earnings adjustment statement adjustment type called ‘Kings Trust’. We will monitor the amounts being claimed.

If the funding rate for the aim is uplifted for area cost and disadvantage you must adjust the additional claim accordingly using the maximum programme values in the table below. Heavy goods vehicle (HGV) driver training

80: The level 2 learning aims that prepare learners for the HGV licence are Ofqual regulated qualifications. These are funded in the same way as other regulated learning aims and can be found on FALA with category code 50.

81: The HGV medical and certificates of professional competence (licence) have their own rates that allow eligible learners to be reimbursed for the cost. The HGV medical has category code 51. The certificates of professional competence (licence) have category code 52.

82: The HGV medical and certificates of professional competence do not attract disadvantage or area cost uplifts, and we do not hold back funding for achievement or completion.

Construction skills certification (CSCS) cards

83: The CSCS cards have their own rates that allow eligible learners to be reimbursed for the cost when delivered alongside specific qualifications. Refer to the Adult skills fund: funding rules for more details.

84: CSCS cards have category code 76. Refer to LARS category codes for more details.

85: CSCS cards do not attract disadvantage and area cost uplifts. We do not hold back funding for achievement or completion.

Our earnings method

Principles

86: The following principles apply to our approach to your earnings:

funding is distributed over the duration of the course starting from the date the learner started

you earn funding for what you deliver, when you deliver it

funding is directly linked to achievement or completion depending on your type of contract and when the learning aim started

for aims funded through a grant contract and started on or after 1 August 2024, funding is directly linked to the learner completing the learning aim or gaining employment

for aims funded through a grant contract and started prior to 1 August 2024, funding is directly linked to the learner achieving the learning aim or gaining employment

for all aims funded through a procured contract funding is directly linked to the learner completing their learning aim and achieving the learning aim (or gaining employment for job outcomes)

Qualifying period for funding

87: If a learner is in learning for at least the qualifying period, we count them as a ‘funding start’. We calculate this from the ‘learning start date’ detailed in the ILR specification. The different qualifying periods are shown in table 5.

Table 5: The qualifying period for funding

Planned length of the learning aim Qualifying period

168 days or more 42 days

14 to 167 days 14 days

Fewer than 14 days 1 day

88: We treat learners as having qualified for funding until a learning actual end date is recorded, at which point we calculate the actual length of the learning aim.

89: If a learner achieves or completes their learning aim in a shorter period than the qualifying period, then we treat them as having qualified.

90: If a learner generates on-programme earnings for passing a census date, then in a subsequent ILR return you record a learning actual end date (without an achievement or completion outcome) that does not meet the qualifying period, we will claw back the funding for that learning aim.

Distribution of funding over time

91: If you are grant-funded, then we will pay you an amount each month based upon the monthly profile in your contract and your allocation value. We then reconcile your funding after the final R14 ILR submission window using your earnings (‘earnings’ are what you have earned through the ILR and EAS submissions you send us). Therefore, for grant-funded providers, your month by month earnings that we calculate will not affect your monthly payments. Rather, it is the overall earnings over the academic year that feed into the reconciliation process.

92: If you are funded through a procured contract, then we will pay you each month in arrears based upon your earnings through your ILR and EAS data. The amount we pay each month may not match your earnings because of:

capping

you have an outstanding debt with us

93: We calculate your earnings each month using the same process and system, regardless of the contract you have with us. We show you these figures through your funding reports (see the funding reports section for more information).

94: We base your earnings on monthly instalments plus an achievement or completion element. The achievement or completion element does not apply to:

work placements

HGV medicals

HGV certificates of competence

CSCS cards

95: We hold back 20% of the weighted rate for each learning aim, which we will only generate when the learner achieves or completes their learning aim. You earn all achievement or completion elements on the learning actual end date recorded on the ILR.

96: We calculate the monthly instalments once we have removed the achievement or completion element (20%). We spread out these instalments over the number of planned months for the learning aim, with a double payment in the first month. The instalment calculation uses the formula ‘n+1’, where ‘n’ is the number of planned months. The formula recognises the upfront costs associated with enrolling a learner on a learning aim.

97: You earn the instalments if the learner is in learning on each census date (the last calendar day of every month). The planned number of months is calculated from the ‘learning start date’ and the ‘learning planned end date’ in the ILR specification.

98: If the learner leaves early, the monthly instalments stop. However, for eligible learners we will pay you a job outcome payment which will be half of the achievement or completion element. If the learner then goes on to achieve or complete the learning aim, you will earn the outstanding monthly instalments and the rest of the achievement or completion element. For more information on job outcomes, refer to the Adult skills fund: funding rules.

99: If a learner leaves before the census date of the first month of learning and the aim has already passed the qualifying period for funding, you will earn the payment relating to this month.

100: Figures 1 and 2 show an example of the earnings method for a learner starting a course in September:

with a planned end date in June

completing or achieving in June

It shows how you earn funding for a course with a total cost of £1,000 over the period of learning:

9 monthly on-programme payments (OPP) of £80, plus an additional monthly OPP of £80 in the first month

an achievement or completion payment of £200

Figure 2: Example of the earnings methodology for all aims funded from a procured contract and aims continuing from 2023 to 2024 funded from a non-procured contract

Recording late data in the ILR

101: If a learner is continuing learning at the final R14 collection at the end of the year, but you record in the subsequent ILR year that they left before 1 August, you may have earned funding that you need to pay back. For example, the funding relating to the funding monitoring report (FRM27 - Continuing or completed learning aims that are now reported as withdrawn on or before 31 July of the previous funding year). In previous years we have asked you to repay the FRM27 funding through the earnings adjustment statement. However, we will now contact you separately after the R14 return to recover the funding that relates to FRM27. You do not need to take any action in-year for this report. Do not submit repayments for FM27 through the EAS.

102: For more information on recording late data in the ILR, refer to ’The impact of incomplete information’ in the ILR provider support manual.

Support funding

Learning support

103: You can access this funding through DWP funded adult skills fund and you record this against a learner’s learning aim in the ILR specification.

104: If you record learning support against a learning aim in the ILR, you will earn a fixed monthly rate of £150. We expect the total you earn from the monthly rate to be enough to cover your costs. If the cost of providing support to a learner exceeds the total earned from the fixed monthly rate, you can claim this excess through the EAS.

105: For learning aims with a planned length of less than one calendar month, our funding calculation will calculate the £150 appropriately in most cases, you should not need to use the EAS to claim the learning support. However, if you see that this funding has not been reflected in your funding reports, and we expect this to be in exceptional cases only, then claim the learning support through the EAS.

106: If learning support is more than £19,000, you can claim exceptional learning support above £19,000 using the cost form. You do not claim the amount above £19,000 through the earnings adjustment statement. The EAS can only be used for claiming the amount up to £19,000 (subtracting what you may have earned through the ILR). For more information, refer to the Adult skills fund: funding rules.

Learner support

107: Learner support is available to provide financial support for learners with a specific financial hardship preventing them from taking part or continuing in learning.

108: Learner support is not formula-funded so you cannot claim it through the ILR. How you claim learner support depends on the contract type the learner requiring support is funded under. If the learner support relates to learning delivered under a:

grant-funded contract, you must complete a mid-year funding forecast, a year-end and final funding claim to receive funding for learner support

procured ASF contract you must claim the support through the EAS

109: For further information, see the earnings adjustment statement and funding claims guidance.

Procured DWP funded ASF provision

110: If you have a contract with us from the most recent adult education budget (AEB) procurement (for delivery from August 2023) you must use the LDM code 388 (‘Adult Education Budget procurement 2023’) for all learning aims in this contract that started for delivery from 1 August 2023. This LDM code distinguishes between our procured and grant-funded contracts so we can identify which contract will pay for provision. Failure to record this code correctly may result in ILR errors or no payments.

114: All learning aims that started before 1 August 2024 and continue into the year 2026 to 2027 should remain being recorded in the ILR using funding model 35 (‘adult skills’). We will merge the information from the calculations for funding model 35 and funding model 38 into a single updated occupancy report, and similarly the funding summary report will contain information from both calculations.
